newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Strong investment support for NZ CBD market -REINZ.
newsitem.headline: Strong investment support for NZ CBD market -REINZ.

text.p: There was strong investment support for central business district (CBD) property over the first quarter, the Real Estate Institute of New Zealand (REINZ) said on Wednesday.
An REINZ informal survey showed support was strongest in Auckland and Wellington.
Personal investment had been the major area of activity, REINZ immediate past president Kent Prier said.
But he said an area of concern was bank base rates of over 11.5 percent -- a disincentive for investors as margins were largely out of line with 90 day bill rates.
"If this continues, the increased cost of borrowing will lower returns on investments and this will have a significant effect on the commercial and investment property market."
As with the last survey, owner-occupier industrial properties had been a major growth area, continuing a medium term trend.
Investment flats performed well, particularly in popular holiday areas such as Rotorua and Hawkes Bay.
Leasing of retail space continued to be influenced by local economies, but remained steady in larger centres.

CBD capitalisation rates in the major centres moved little with Auckland between 7.5 and 10.5 percent, Wellington 7.5 and 11 percent, 9.5 and 11.0 percent in Christchurch and Dunedin between 10 and 12 percent.
In Auckland, industrial properties had been in demand with agents reporting high levels of sales and leasings.
Enquiries for CBD commercial properties were outstripping supply, while the incentives for tenants seemed to be drying up.
Office space remained steady with the CBD being the main area of support.
In Wellington interest in commercial properties remained high with steady supply pointing to a firm market.
